# mongosh Reference — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for mongosh Reference. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Interactive mongosh output is not a stable substitute for JSON serialization: compatibility documentation describes unquoted keys and single-quoted strings. Use EJSON.stringify() for explicit Extended JSON output; the upstream CLI also documents --json=canonical or --json=relaxed for --eval results. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/compatibility.md · keywords: mongosh Reference · also: https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongosh

## Structure and components

- [statement] mongosh is the MongoDB shell implemented in a Node.js-based environment; its upstream repository contains components for the REPL, browser and Compass environments. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongosh · keywords: mongosh Reference · also: https://studio3t.com/knowledge-base/3t-build/desktop-ide/studio-3t-now-defaults-to-the-mongosh-shell/
- [statement] displayBatchSize controls the number of items shown per cursor iteration; cursor.batchSize() controls the documents returned per server batch. These settings address different layers. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/compatibility.md

## How it works

- [statement] The script guide recommends --file or -f explicitly because bare filenames can cause connection parsing failures when combined with other command-line arguments; load() has no search path. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md
- [statement] Legacy mongo scripts need migration review: numeric values default to Int32 when representable and otherwise Double in mongosh, whereas the legacy shell defaulted to Double. Mixing shells can therefore change stored BSON types. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/compatibility.md
- [statement] When a script establishes its own connection, --nodb prevents the shell from making its initial connection on startup. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md · keywords: mongosh Reference · also: https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongosh

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use mongosh --file script.js (or -f) for command-line scripts, and load("script.js") within an existing shell session. The CLI supports executing scripts without entering the interactive console. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md · keywords: mongosh Reference · also: https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongosh, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/cheatsheet.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Legacy-shell migration requires script review. Studio 3T identifies native JavaScript function changes, Percona warns that legacy methods can be unavailable or replaced, and MongoDB enumerates deprecated helpers. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/compatibility.md · keywords: mongosh Reference · also: https://studio3t.com/knowledge-base/3t-build/desktop-ide/studio-3t-now-defaults-to-the-mongosh-shell/, https://learn.percona.com/hubfs/Webinars/2023/March22-end-of-life-is-coming-for-mongoDB-4.2/End%20of%20Life%20is%20Coming%20for%20MongoDB%204_2%20%20How%20to%20Upgrade_v4.pptx.pdf
- [statement] Database-call results cannot be used in ordinary class constructors, non-async generators, Array.sort callbacks or class setters as if all JavaScript contexts supported shell database evaluation. The compatibility reference gives async or precomputation alternatives. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/compatibility.md
- [statement] Studio 3T's October 2022 migration announcement states that Query Assist support introduced in 2022.9 required its bundled mongosh; non-bundled mongosh lacked Query Assist and inline editing in that integration. This is historical product-specific behavior, not a current universal mongosh limitation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2022-10-31) — https://studio3t.com/knowledge-base/3t-build/desktop-ide/studio-3t-now-defaults-to-the-mongosh-shell/
- [statement] In Microsoft's Azure migration troubleshooting procedure, successful TCP connectivity followed by mongosh TLS or authentication failure directs investigation to certificate settings or credentials/authentication database. The probe must run from the relevant network position; success from an arbitrary workstation does not establish migration-service reachability. (low confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/documentdb/troubleshoot-connectivity

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The official cheat sheet is explicitly incomplete; full coverage requires the Database Commands and mongosh Methods references. Import/export and dump/restore utilities run in the system terminal rather than as mongosh methods. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/cheatsheet.md
- [statement] A historical July 2023 VS Code issue reports CommandNotFoundException for mongosh despite a working executable elsewhere. It establishes an integration launch symptom, without proving its cause or a current product defect. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb-js/vscode/issues/568
- [statement] To make administrative scripts portable, select the database with db.getSiblingDB("name") and supply host and port on the command line rather than embedding a deployment address in the script. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md · keywords: mongosh Reference · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/cheatsheet.md
- [statement] mongoimport, mongoexport, mongodump and mongorestore are separate Database Tools commands executed in the system terminal, rather than mongosh methods. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/cheatsheet.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A connection URI or --host/--port selects the deployment; --username and --authenticationDatabase select authentication details, and omitting the password allows an interactive prompt. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/cheatsheet.md · keywords: mongosh Reference · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/connect.md
- [statement] For portable scripts, select the database with db.getSiblingDB() and supply deployment details on the command line. If the script creates its own connection, --nodb avoids an initial automatic connection. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md
- [statement] mongosh reads .mongoshrc.js from the user's home directory on startup; --norc suppresses that startup file. A legacy .mongorc.js is not automatically loaded as a substitute. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md · keywords: mongosh Reference · also: https://github.com/mongodb-js/mongosh, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/compatibility.md
- [statement] Built-in .editor mode accepts multiline code: Ctrl-D runs the code and Ctrl-C cancels it; declarations remain in the shell’s global scope afterward. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/editor-mode.md
- [statement] MongoDB documents try/catch with exit(code) for scripts that must terminate after exceptions or unexpected results. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md
- [statement] For connection checks, db.runCommand({ping: 1}) is a concrete shell probe; Microsoft demonstrates running it noninteractively with mongosh "$SOURCE_URI" --eval and expects { ok: 1 }. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/cheatsheet.md · keywords: mongosh Reference · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/documentdb/troubleshoot-connectivity
- [statement] load() accepts relative and absolute paths but has no search path: a relative script must exist under the shell's current working directory at the supplied path. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/write-scripts.md
- [statement] The compatibility reference deprecates count(), insert(), remove(), save() and update() in favor of explicit methods such as countDocuments()/estimatedDocumentCount(), insertOne()/insertMany(), deleteOne()/deleteMany(), and updateOne()/updateMany(). (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell/reference/compatibility.md
